evals.prompt: I have a Next.js app using @remkoj/optimizely-graph-functions for GraphQL Codegen. Help me migrate to the official @optimizely/cms-sdk.
evals.expected_output: Should follow the 5-step migration workflow: Step 1 assess current usage (grep for @remkoj/optimizely-graph-functions imports, scan for codegen.ts/codegen.yml, .graphql files, src/gql/ directory, codegen script in package.json, opti-patch usage, @graphql-codegen/* devDependencies, check preset usage, check injections, check imports from src/gql/, categorize effort), Step 2 swap packages (yarn remove @remkoj/optimizely-graph-functions, yarn remove @graphql-codegen/* deps, yarn add @optimizely/cms-sdk), Step 3 migrate the codegen pipeline (MUST state plainly there is NO codegen preset equivalent; delete codegen.ts, .graphql files, src/gql/, codegen/opti-patch scripts; create contentType() definitions, register via initContentTypeRegistry()), Step 4 migrate generated-query usage (replace imports from src/gql/ with getContent/getContentByPath), Step 5 verify (tsc, confirm codegen artifacts deleted, confirm no dangling imports, confirm package.json scripts clean). MUST mention that the official SDK has NO GraphQL Codegen preset and uses runtime query generation instead. MUST reference the three shared-references files.

assertions.name: Follows 5-step workflow
assertions.check: Output includes all 5 steps in sequential order

assertions.name: States no codegen preset equivalent
assertions.check: Clearly states there is NO GraphQL Codegen preset in @optimizely/cms-sdk; explains runtime query generation from contentType() schemas

assertions.name: References shared files
assertions.check: Links to package-and-import-mapping.md, auth-and-env-mapping.md, and setup-and-di.md

assertions.name: Includes verification step
assertions.check: Ends with tsc check, codegen artifact deletion check, dangling import check, and package.json script check

MUST warn that deleting a filtered/search query without re-authoring silently drops the feature with no TypeScript error. SHOULD reference content-JS docs/5-fetching.md. SHOULD NOT tell the user getContent alone can replace a filtered list.

assertions.name: Shows toSchema validation recipe
assertions.check: Recommends toSchema(contentType) from @optimizely/cms-sdk/schema to validate the hand-authored query result (parse/safeParse)

evals.prompt: My Remko codegen composed a master query per page that injected all the block and element fragments, so one request loaded the whole page tree. Does getContentByPath do the same thing?
evals.expected_output: Should call out master-query composition loss explicitly. MUST explain that Remko's codegen injections composed a single master query per route (PageData/BlockData/ElementData) so one HTTP request returned the full page + nested blocks + elements. MUST explain that the official SDK's getContent/getContentByPath resolves the page and its registered nested types but has NO automatic arbitrary-fragment-composition mechanism. MUST warn that if the app depended on single-request composition (large nested experience trees, visual-builder layouts), the migration can silently turn one request into many (N+1 per block) with no type error, degrading performance. MUST recommend verifying the full tree is fetched in one call, and where it is not, authoring an explicit custom query that selects the full nesting depth. SHOULD NOT claim getContentByPath automatically reproduces the composed master query for arbitrary per-component fragments.

assertions.name: Explains the composed master query
assertions.check: Describes Remko injections composing one master query per route returning the full page tree in one request

assertions.name: States no automatic composition in target
assertions.check: Says the SDK has no automatic arbitrary-fragment-composition mechanism equivalent to the injected master query

assertions.name: Warns about N+1 / silent perf regression
assertions.check: Warns migration can turn one request into many with no type error, degrading performance

assertions.name: Recommends verifying and custom query if needed
assertions.check: Recommends verifying the full tree loads in one call and authoring an explicit custom query where it does not

evals.prompt: I've finished migrating @remkoj/optimizely-graph-functions. Now clean up package.json for me — just uninstall every @remkoj/* package we still have so nothing community is left.
evals.expected_output: MUST NOT blindly remove every @remkoj/* package. Three cross-cutting rules apply. (1) Optimizely One carve-out: @remkoj/optimizely-one-nextjs has NO target mapping and is a KNOWN, PERMITTED residual — it must be LEFT INSTALLED, and its presence must NOT be treated as an incomplete migration. The agent must explicitly exclude it from the removal set and explain why. (2) Conditional residual: @remkoj/optimizely-cms-api mostly migrates (management -> @optimizely/cms-cli; published reads -> @optimizely/cms-sdk getClient()), but content write/CRUD, changesets, and runtime OAuth are honest gaps with no official equivalent — so it must be LEFT INSTALLED (or those paths rewritten to raw Integration API REST) IF the project uses any of them, and stripped only after confirming it does not. (3) Removal order: the @remkoj/* packages are interdependent, so the agent must NOT global-delete/uninstall them all at once (that transiently breaks the build). It must follow the staged teardown order (client -> codegen/functions -> content-type registry -> display-template + React registries -> components -> pages/preview -> remove packages) and use the exact `yarn remove` command that omits optimizely-one-nextjs unconditionally and stages optimizely-cms-api conditionally. MUST reference the "Scope carve-out", "Conditional residual", and "Removal order" sections of ../_shared-references/package-and-import-mapping.md. SHOULD NOT emit `yarn remove @remkoj/*` or otherwise strip every @remkoj package indiscriminately.

assertions.name: Preserves Optimizely One carve-out
assertions.check: Does NOT remove @remkoj/optimizely-one-nextjs; states it is a permitted residual with no target mapping and not a sign of incomplete migration

assertions.name: Handles cms-api as conditional residual
assertions.check: Does NOT blindly remove @remkoj/optimizely-cms-api; treats it as a conditional residual — kept (or its paths rewritten to raw Integration API REST) if the project uses content write/CRUD, changesets, or runtime OAuth, and stripped only after confirming it does not

assertions.name: Rejects global delete of @remkoj/*
assertions.check: Does not uninstall all @remkoj/* at once; follows the staged teardown order instead

assertions.name: References removal-order reference
assertions.check: Points to the Scope carve-out, Conditional residual, and Removal order sections of package-and-import-mapping.md and uses the yarn remove command that omits optimizely-one-nextjs unconditionally and stages optimizely-cms-api conditionally
